question.problem:
What is the missing part of the expression below?

$$
\frac{4}{19}=\frac{\bbox[1pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}}{-19}
$$
question.worked_solution:
A positive number can be obtained if we divide two numbers that are either both positive or both negative.

So, given a positive fraction, we have the following equivalent notations:

$$
\frac{4}{19}=\frac{-4}{-19}
$$

In our case, we see that the denominator on the right-hand side is negative $(-19).$ Therefore, the missing numerator must be $(-4):$

$$
\frac{4}{19}=\frac{-4}{-19}
$$
